questions.text_english:
Read the following text:

(1) Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) is now high on the international agenda and ESD is seen as a way to encourage greater sustainable consumption and production, to counter the effects of climate change, address threats to biodiversity and provide more effective disaster risk reduction. Education for Sustainable Development is seen by UN as a lifelong process from early childhood to higher and adult education and goes beyond formal education. As values, lifestyles and attitudes are established from an early age, the role of education is of particular importance for children! ESD has often been associated with curriculum projects linked with recycling; energy and water conservation; pollution reduction and sustainable consumption — all developed to contribute towards achieving a more sustainable future.

(2) Research from developmental psychology, longitudinal studies, social-cultural analysis, and neuroscience have all shown that it is in the early years that children have the greatest capacity to learn, and it is in these years that many of our fundamental attitudes and values are first put into place. Children are already investigating issues related to recycling, energy conservation, waste disposal and changes in their local environment. ESD in Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) is of great significance. The development of ESD and ECCE requires more than just curriculum development. It provides the possibility of a transformational reconstruction.

(3) UNICEF reports show that children under the age of eight represent the highest percentage of affected population in today's global emergencies. A UNESCO survey has shown that the ministries of education, environment and sustainable development in 97 UN member states identify poverty as the highest priority area to be addressed in achieving sustainable development. In fact, reductions in poverty and inequality are widely recognised as the priority in efforts to create a more sustainable world. At a global level, millions of children start school carrying the handicap that comes with the experience of malnutrition, ill-health and poverty. Yet, equitable access to high-quality pre-school programmes remain a problem in both rich and poor countries. Sustainable development projects that enable rapid progress in maternal health, child nutrition and survival already exist, even in some of the world's poorest countries. Linking health and education agenda has been recognised as extremely important.
questions.instruction_line: Read the following text and answer the questions based on the passage above.
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following text and answer the questions based on the passage above.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the following with a suitable explanation with reference to paragraph (1).

ESD is now high on the international agenda because _______.

fill_values: it is seen as a way to encourage greater sustainable consumption and production, counter climate change, address threats to biodiversity, and provide more effective disaster risk reduction

sub_questions.solution: ESD is now high on the international agenda because it is seen as a way to encourage greater sustainable consumption and production, to counter the effects of climate change, address threats to biodiversity, and provide more effective disaster risk reduction.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the given passage, how does UN view ESD as a lifelong process? What are the critical areas of emphasis? (Paragraph 1)

key_points: UN sees ESD as a lifelong process from early childhood to higher and adult education that goes beyond formal education.
Critical areas of emphasis include recycling, energy and water conservation, pollution reduction, and sustainable consumption.

sub_questions.solution: The UN views ESD as a lifelong process that spans from early childhood through higher and adult education, extending well beyond the boundaries of formal schooling. The UN recognises that values and attitudes are shaped from an early age, making children a critical focus. The key areas of emphasis include curriculum projects linked to recycling, energy and water conservation, pollution reduction, and sustainable consumption, all aimed at building a more sustainable future.

sub_questions.text_english: List two curriculum projects that ESD (Education for Sustainable Development) has been linked with. (Paragraph 1)

key_points: Recycling
Energy and water conservation

sub_questions.solution: ESD has been linked with curriculum projects related to (1) recycling, and (2) energy and water conservation. These projects are developed to contribute towards achieving a more sustainable future.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the following suitably:

Many of our fundamental attitudes and values are put into place in the early years as _______. (Paragraph 2)

fill_values: research from developmental psychology, longitudinal studies, social-cultural analysis, and neuroscience shows that children have the greatest capacity to learn in their early years

sub_questions.solution: Many of our fundamental attitudes and values are put into place in the early years as research from developmental psychology, longitudinal studies, social-cultural analysis, and neuroscience has shown that children have the greatest capacity to learn during this period.

sub_questions.text_english:
Substitute the underlined word with the correct word from paragraph (2):

ESD in Early Childhood Care and Education provides the possibility of transformational reconstruction.
(A) positive change
(B) power to reform
(C) negative impact
(D) creative
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) positive change. The word 'transformational' in the passage means bringing about a fundamental and significant change, which most closely aligns with 'positive change'. Option B is partially relevant but does not capture the full meaning. Options C and D are clearly incorrect as the passage has a positive and constructive tone throughout.

sub_questions.text_english:
What do UNICEF reports reveal about the vulnerability of children under the age of eight during global emergencies? (Paragraph 3)
(A) UNICEF reports highlight the resilience of children under the age of eight during global emergencies.
(B) UNICEF reports indicate that children under the age of eight are rarely affected by global emergencies.
(C) UNICEF reports show that children under the age of eight represent the highest percentage of affected population in global emergencies.
(D) UNICEF reports suggest that children under the age of eight are primarily responsible for responding to global emergencies.

options_english.A: UNICEF reports highlight the resilience of children under the age of eight during global emergencies.
options_english.B: UNICEF reports indicate that children under the age of eight are rarely affected by global emergencies.
options_english.C: UNICEF reports show that children under the age of eight represent the highest percentage of affected population in global emergencies.
options_english.D: UNICEF reports suggest that children under the age of eight are primarily responsible for responding to global emergencies.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Paragraph 3 explicitly states that UNICEF reports show children under the age of eight represent the highest percentage of the affected population in today's global emergencies. Options A and B contradict the passage, and Option D is entirely unsupported by the text.

sub_questions.text_english: What remains a problem in both rich and poor countries? What has been recognised as crucial? (Paragraph 3)

key_points: Equitable access to high-quality pre-school programmes remains a problem in both rich and poor countries.
Linking the health and education agenda has been recognised as crucial.

sub_questions.solution: Equitable access to high-quality pre-school programmes remains a problem in both rich and poor countries. Linking the health and education agenda has been recognised as extremely crucial to achieving sustainable development.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the sentence with the correct response:

The writer's tone in the passage is _______.
sub_questions.solution: The writer's tone in the passage is informative and concerned. Throughout the passage, the writer presents factual data from UNICEF, UNESCO, and research studies while expressing concern about the vulnerability of children and the need for immediate attention to sustainable development in education.

questions.text_english:
Read the following text:

(1) Electric vehicles (EV) market is growing rapidly all over the world. In India also the EV market has gained significant momentum. It has grown more after the implementation of FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacture of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles) scheme in 2015 by Ministry of Heavy Industry and Public Enterprises.

(2) Electric vehicles are solutions to be independent and free from imported energy resources. Electric cars can bring a major change to India in becoming self-sustainable. EV could also be the alternative to decrease carbon dioxide gas. Carbon dioxide from automobiles is one of the causes of air pollution.

(3) An EV can be used for flexible load, for standardizing the grid with substantial share of fluctuating renewable energy generation. EV emits 30-80% less greenhouse gas when compared with Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicle. EVs do not consume any energy when it is stationary as compared to ICE vehicles where fuel is consumed when it is idle. EV is recognised as promising alternatives to vehicles and will potentially replace ICE vehicles in the near future.

(4) The electric vehicles have low emissions, high efficiency and smooth operation. The energy consumption and emissions for plug in hybrid electric vehicles found that compared to gasoline vehicles there is 37.5% less energy consumption and 35% less greenhouse gas emissions.

The government have started financial policies to encourage EV adoption; however, decision makers have to plan a long-term perspective to get them implemented efficiently.
questions.instruction_line: Read the following text and answer the questions based on the passage above.
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following text and answer the questions based on the passage above.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
What does the phrase 'gained significant momentum' in paragraph (1) tell us about the impact of EV market?
(A) It is momentarily important
(B) It has developed very quickly
(C) It has gained profit
(D) It has to develop a significant market

options_english.D: It has to develop a significant market

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) It has developed very quickly. The phrase 'gained significant momentum' means that the EV market in India has grown rapidly and built considerable speed in its development. Option A is incorrect as momentum implies sustained growth, not temporary importance. Options C and D are not supported by the context of the phrase.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that is true for the Assertion and Reason given below:

Assertion: Electric vehicles can bring a major change to India.
Reason: It can bring India to becoming self-sustainable.

(A) Both the Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
(B) Both the Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
(C) The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
(D) The Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

options_english.A: Both the Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options_english.B: Both the Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options_english.C: The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
options_english.D: The Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Paragraph 2 of the passage directly states that electric cars can bring a major change to India in becoming self-sustainable, confirming that self-sustainability is indeed the reason for the major change EVs can bring.

sub_questions.text_english: Give two benefits of using Electric vehicles over Internal Combustion Engine vehicles.

key_points: EVs emit 30-80% less greenhouse gas compared to ICE vehicles.
EVs do not consume any energy when stationary, unlike ICE vehicles which consume fuel even when idle.

sub_questions.solution: Two major benefits of Electric Vehicles over ICE vehicles are: First, EVs emit 30 to 80 percent less greenhouse gas compared to Internal Combustion Engine vehicles, making them far more environmentally friendly. Second, EVs do not consume any energy when stationary, whereas ICE vehicles continue to burn fuel even when idle, making EVs significantly more energy-efficient in real-world usage.

sub_questions.text_english: With reference to the passage, the word 'idle' in paragraph (3) most nearly means _______.
sub_questions.solution: The word 'idle' in paragraph (3) most nearly means stationary or not moving. In the context of the passage, it refers to a vehicle that is running but not in motion, consuming fuel without performing any work, in contrast to EVs which consume no energy in such a state.

sub_questions.text_english: How do electric vehicles contribute to diminishing a country's reliance on imported energy?

key_points: Electric vehicles are solutions to be independent and free from imported energy resources, helping the country become self-sustainable.

sub_questions.solution: Electric vehicles help diminish a country's reliance on imported energy because they run on electricity, which can be generated domestically through various sources. As stated in paragraph 2, EVs offer solutions to become independent and free from imported energy resources, thus enabling a country like India to become self-sustainable.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the given prompt and select the correct option in the brackets to fill in the blank:

EV could be the alternative to _______ (enhance / reduce) the carbon dioxide gas emission.
sub_questions.solution: The correct word is 'reduce'. According to paragraph 2, EVs could be the alternative to decrease carbon dioxide gas emissions from automobiles, which are one of the causes of air pollution. 'Enhance' is the opposite of the intended meaning and is therefore incorrect.

sub_questions.text_english: Give evidence from the passage to show that government is encouraging the use of Electric Vehicles.

key_points: The government implemented the FAME scheme in 2015 and has started financial policies to encourage EV adoption.

sub_questions.solution: The passage provides two pieces of evidence showing government encouragement of EV use. First, the FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacture of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles) scheme was implemented in 2015 by the Ministry of Heavy Industry and Public Enterprises. Second, paragraph 4 states that the government has started financial policies specifically to encourage EV adoption.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the sentence suitably:

The result of the implementation of FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacture of Electric vehicles) is _______.

fill_values: that the EV market in India has gained significant momentum and grown rapidly

sub_questions.solution: The result of the implementation of FAME is that the EV market in India has gained significant momentum and has grown rapidly. As mentioned in paragraph 1, after the launch of the FAME scheme in 2015, the electric vehicle market in India expanded considerably.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the following with a suitable reason:

The long-term perspective by decision makers is to ensure _______.

fill_values: that the financial policies encouraging EV adoption are implemented efficiently

sub_questions.solution: The long-term perspective by decision makers is to ensure that the financial policies encouraging EV adoption are implemented efficiently. Paragraph 4 states that while the government has started financial policies, decision makers must plan with a long-term view to get them implemented in an effective manner.

questions.solution: Grammar tasks. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the newspaper report by using the correct form of the verb given in the bracket:

He was a renowned business person. He _______ (purchase) a house in the city last year.
sub_questions.solution: The correct form is 'purchased'. Since the sentence describes an action completed at a specific time in the past ('last year'), the Simple Past Tense is required. The verb 'purchase' in simple past becomes 'purchased'. The complete sentence reads: He purchased a house in the city last year.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete the concluding part of an article on 'Exploitation of Children':

It _______ (may/should/could) be our concerted effort not to employ children in industries and to save them from any kind of exploitation.
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is 'should'. The modal verb 'should' expresses moral obligation or duty, which is appropriate here as the sentence is making a strong recommendation about collective responsibility to protect children from exploitation. 'May' expresses possibility and 'could' expresses ability, neither of which conveys the necessary sense of duty required in this context.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the given line and identify the error. Also provide the correct word.

Mobile phones has become an integral part of life.
sub_questions.solution: The error is 'has' and the correction is 'have'. The subject 'Mobile phones' is plural, so the verb must agree with it in number. The rule of subject-verb agreement requires a plural subject to take a plural verb. The corrected sentence reads: Mobile phones have become an integral part of life.

sub_questions.text_english:
Take a look at the conversation between two friends Riya and Simran discussing a book that one of them has recently read.

Riya: The book really caught my attention. It's called 'Eternal Echoes'.
Simran: Sounds interesting! I'll definitely add it to my reading list. Thanks for the recommendation!

Select the correct option to complete the reporting of the above dialogue.

Riya told Simran about the book called Eternal Echoes that had captured her interest. Simran, in response, expressed that it _______ and mentioned that she would consider reading it.
(A) sound interesting
(B) sounded interesting
(C) will be interesting
(D) was found to be interesting
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 'sounded interesting'. In reported speech, when the reporting verb is in the past tense ('expressed'), the verb in the reported clause must also shift to the past tense. 'Sounds' (simple present) becomes 'sounded' (simple past) in reported speech. Option A is in present tense which is grammatically incorrect. Options C and D do not correctly reflect the original dialogue.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the line given below:

He usually ate breakfast before he goes to school.

Options | Error | Correction
(A) | usually | always
(B) | ate | eats
(C) | before | after
(D) | goes | went
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B): Error is 'ate' and correction is 'eats'. The sentence describes a habitual action ('usually'), which requires the Simple Present Tense. The word 'goes' in the second clause is already in Simple Present, so the first clause must also be in Simple Present. Therefore, 'ate' (Simple Past) should be corrected to 'eats'. The corrected sentence reads: He usually eats breakfast before he goes to school.

sub_questions.text_english:
Report the dialogue between a teacher and a student by completing the sentence:

Teacher: Good morning! Today, we're going to learn about the importance of trees. They play a vital role in our ecosystem. Can you think of any other reasons?
Student: I pledge to plant some trees this weekend.

The student understood the importance of trees and added that he _______.

fill_values: pledged to plant some trees that weekend

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is 'pledged to plant some trees that weekend'. In reported speech, the reporting verb shifts to past tense ('pledged' from 'pledge'), and time expressions change ('this weekend' becomes 'that weekend'). The complete reported sentence reads: The student understood the importance of trees and added that he pledged to plant some trees that weekend.

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply correction for the given sentence talking about importance of a 'Sound Sleep'.

Sleep is important in maintain one's health and well being.
sub_questions.solution: The error is 'maintain' and the correction is 'maintaining'. After the preposition 'in', a gerund (verb+ing form) must be used, not the base form of the verb. This is the rule governing preposition + gerund usage. The corrected sentence reads: Sleep is important in maintaining one's health and well-being.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the given narrative, by filling the blank with the correct option:

When they began to play it _______ to rain.
(A) start
(B) started
(C) starts
(D) having started
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 'started'. The sentence is written in the past tense as indicated by 'began', and the narrative describes a sequence of past events. The verb in the second clause must also be in the Simple Past Tense to maintain tense consistency. Therefore, 'started' is the correct choice. Options A and C are in the present tense, and option D is grammatically incorrect in this context.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank choosing the most appropriate option:

The teacher distributed a piece of paper to _______ student.
(A) few
(B) all
(C) many
(D) each
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 'each'. The sentence uses the singular noun 'student' and a singular verb form, which requires a singular determiner. 'Each' is used with singular countable nouns and means every individual one. 'Few', 'all', and 'many' are used with plural nouns, making them grammatically incorrect with the singular 'student'.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option, to complete the line given below:

Oral hygiene _______ be inculcated in children early in life. (should, would)
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is 'should'. The modal verb 'should' is used to express advice, recommendation, or moral obligation. Here, the sentence is advising that oral hygiene ought to be taught to children from an early age, which conveys a sense of duty and recommendation. 'Would' expresses willingness or a conditional action, which does not fit the meaning of the sentence.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the given sentence by selecting the correct option:

The information given here _______ to all the products in this section.
(A) apply
(B) applied
(C) is applied
(D) applies
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 'applies'. The subject 'The information' is singular and the sentence describes a general truth or current fact, which requires Simple Present Tense with a third-person singular verb. 'Applies' correctly agrees with the singular subject. Option A 'apply' is the plural form, option B 'applied' is past tense, and option C 'is applied' implies passive voice which changes the meaning.

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply correction for the following sentence:

Be the changes you want to see in the world.

fill_values: Error: Be | Correction: Be (no error — or — 'changes' should be 'change')

sub_questions.solution: The error is 'changes' and the correction is 'change'. The famous quotation reads 'Be the change you want to see in the world.' The noun 'change' should be singular here as the imperative sentence refers to a singular abstract concept of transformation. Using 'changes' (plural) is grammatically and contextually incorrect. The corrected sentence reads: Be the change you want to see in the world.

sub_questions.text_english: You are Sonia / Sonu, residing at 67/98 Malkaganj, Sonepat. Compose a letter in about 120 words to the Head Librarian of your child's school drawing attention to the poor library facilities. Give suggestions on how things can be improved to inculcate reading habits among children.

key_points: Format: Sender's address, date, recipient's designation, subject line
Opening: State the purpose of writing — poor library facilities
Body: Describe the problems observed in the school library
Suggestions: Recommend improvements to encourage reading habits
Closing: Polite request for prompt action and complimentary close

sub_questions.solution:
67/98, Malkaganj,
Sonepat
7th June, 2024

The Head Librarian,
[School Name],
Sonepat

Subject: Poor Library Facilities and Suggestions for Improvement

Dear Sir/Ma'am,

I am Sonia, parent of a student in Class VI of your school. I am writing to draw your kind attention to the inadequate library facilities available to our children. The library has a very limited collection of books, insufficient seating, and poor lighting, which discourages students from spending time there.

I would like to suggest that the library be stocked with age-appropriate storybooks, magazines, and encyclopaedias. Comfortable seating and proper lighting should be arranged. A weekly free-reading period could be introduced to build reading habits. A book recommendation board could also motivate children to read.

I sincerely hope you will consider these suggestions.

Yours sincerely,
Sonia

sub_questions.text_english: As Sharmila Sahani, a conscientious resident of 25/22, Rajpur, Fahetabad, you have recently come across numerous newspaper articles featuring tragic incidents where lives have been lost due to reckless driving and not following the traffic rules. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily, shedding light on this issue and give suggestions on what can be done.

key_points: Format: Sender's address, date, 'To the Editor', subject line
Opening: Introduce the issue of reckless driving and traffic violations
Body: Highlight the severity of the problem with reference to newspaper reports
Suggestions: Stricter enforcement, awareness campaigns, traffic education in schools
Closing: Appeal for public awareness and complimentary close

sub_questions.solution:
25/22, Rajpur,
Fahetabad
7th June, 2024

The Editor,
[Name of National Daily],
New Delhi

Subject: Reckless Driving — A Growing Menace on Indian Roads

Dear Sir/Ma'am,

Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to highlight the alarming rise in accidents caused by reckless driving and non-compliance with traffic rules. As a concerned citizen, I have read numerous reports of tragic deaths that could have been prevented.

Drivers frequently jump red lights, use mobile phones while driving, and exceed speed limits without fear of consequences. I urge the authorities to enforce stricter penalties, increase police patrolling, and install more surveillance cameras. Traffic safety education should be made compulsory in schools. Awareness campaigns through media can also help.

I hope your newspaper will champion this important cause.

Yours sincerely,
Sharmila Sahani

questions.solution: Analytical paragraph writing. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Today, many projects in India are being initiated and implemented with the aim of transforming India into a digitally empowered society and economy.

Digital India Program:
IT – Jobs
E – governance
E – Kranti Electronic Delivery of Services
Broadband for all – Urban and Rural
Information for all.

Write an analytical paragraph of 100-120 words based on the given information.

key_points: Introduction: Introduce the Digital India Programme and its goal
IT Jobs and E-governance as key pillars
E-Kranti for electronic delivery of services
Broadband for all — bridging the urban-rural divide
Conclusion: Significance of Information for all in building a digital society

sub_questions.solution: The Digital India Programme is a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at transforming the country into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. One of its most significant components is the creation of IT jobs, which provides employment opportunities to millions of young Indians in the technology sector. E-governance ensures that government services are delivered transparently and efficiently to citizens through digital platforms. The E-Kranti initiative focuses on the electronic delivery of essential services such as healthcare, education, and banking to every citizen. Broadband for all ensures that both urban and rural populations have equal access to the internet, bridging the digital divide. Finally, the goal of 'Information for all' guarantees that every citizen can access government data and services online, fostering an inclusive and empowered digital India.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the given details of the different activities that interest children in the age group of 14-17 years.
- dance, music, art
- outdoor sports like cricket, hockey, basketball, soccer, tennis
- computer games
- net surfing
- social media

Analyse the details and write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words about the suitability of the given activities. Focus on factors like interest, physical, mental and emotional development, personality development, and suitability.

key_points: Introduction: Overview of activities for the 14-17 age group
Physical activities (sports) and their benefits for health and teamwork
Creative activities (dance, music, art) and emotional/personality development
Digital activities (net surfing, social media, computer games) and their concerns
Conclusion: Balanced approach is most suitable

sub_questions.solution: Children in the age group of 14-17 years are drawn to a wide variety of activities, each offering different developmental benefits. Outdoor sports like cricket, hockey, basketball, soccer, and tennis are highly suitable as they promote physical fitness, teamwork, discipline, and mental resilience. Creative pursuits such as dance, music, and art are excellent for emotional expression, personality development, and building self-confidence. However, activities like computer games, net surfing, and social media, while entertaining, pose significant concerns for this age group. Excessive screen time can hamper concentration, disrupt sleep, and affect mental health. Social media may also expose teenagers to cyberbullying and unrealistic standards. Therefore, while all activities have their place, a balanced approach that prioritises physical and creative engagement is most suitable for the holistic development of young adolescents.

questions.solution: Extract-based questions. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract A: "Paper has more patience than people. I thought of this saying on one of those days when I was feeling a little depressed and was sitting at home with my chin in my hands, bored and listless, wondering whether to stay in or go out. I finally stayed where I was, brooding: Yes, paper does have more patience, and since I'm not planning to let anyone else read this stiff backed notebook grandly referred to as a 'diary', unless I should ever find a real friend, it probably won't make a bit of difference." (From the Diary of Anne Frank)

In light of the excerpt, what can we infer about the speaker's emotional state?

key_points: Anne Frank is feeling depressed, lonely, and bored, and she lacks a true friend to confide in.

sub_questions.solution: From the excerpt, we can infer that Anne Frank is in a state of depression, loneliness, and emotional restlessness. She sits idle, bored, and listless, unable to decide what to do. Her reference to not having a real friend and her reliance on a diary for emotional release reveals deep inner loneliness and a longing for genuine companionship.

sub_questions.text_english:
The narrator enhances the narrative technique of the extract by using:
(A) descriptive language
(B) literary allusions
(C) humour
(D) reflective
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) reflective. Throughout the extract, Anne Frank contemplates her own feelings, the nature of paper versus people, and her desire for a true friend. The tone is introspective and self-examining, which is characteristic of reflective writing. Option A is partially true but not the dominant technique; B and C are not evident in the extract.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank with the correct word from the bracket:

The narrator doesn't plan to let anyone read her diary as she doesn't have any real _______. (friend / incidents)
sub_questions.solution: The correct word is 'friend'. Anne Frank explicitly states in the extract that she won't let anyone read her diary unless she ever finds a real friend. This shows that she does not share her diary because she lacks a true and trustworthy friend to confide in. 'Incidents' is irrelevant to the context.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the narrator say that 'paper has more patience than people'?

key_points: Anne says this because paper silently listens to everything without judging or responding, unlike real people who may not be as patient or understanding.

sub_questions.solution: Anne Frank says 'paper has more patience than people' because she feels that a diary silently accepts all her thoughts, feelings, and confessions without judgement or impatience. Unlike people, who may dismiss or misunderstand her, paper listens without interruption. This reflects her loneliness and her inability to find a truly patient and understanding human companion.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract B: "He was silent, stupefied, in dismay, at the sight of his wife weeping. He stammered, 'What is the matter? What is the matter?' By a violent effort, she had controlled her vexation and responded in a calm voice, wiping her moist cheeks, 'Nothing. Only I have no dress and consequently I cannot go to this affair. Give your card to some colleague whose wife is better fitted out than I.' He was grieved, but answered, 'Let us see, Matilda. How much would a suitable costume cost, something that would serve for their occasions, something very simple?' She reflected for some seconds thinking of a sum that could ask for without bringing with it an immediate refusal and a frightened exclamation from the economical clerk." (The Necklace)

What can we infer about Matilda's emotions and financial situation based on her husband's reaction and her response to not having a dress for the affair?

key_points: Matilda is emotionally distressed and deeply unhappy about her lack of a suitable dress.
The financial situation is tight — she must calculate a sum carefully so as not to alarm her 'economical' husband.

sub_questions.solution: From the extract, we can infer that Matilda is deeply distressed and dissatisfied with her financial circumstances. Her weeping and suppressed vexation reveal her strong desire to attend the affair dressed well, which her modest means do not allow. Her husband's careful inquiry about cost and her own deliberate calculation of a sum that would not shock him reveal that the family lives on a tight budget with very little room for extravagance.

sub_questions.text_english:
Which of the following is NOT a reason for Matilda's distress in the extract?
(A) She has no suitable dress for the affair.
(B) She is upset about her husband's reaction.
(C) She is worried about the cost of a suitable costume.
(D) The card did not bear her name.

options_english.A: She has no suitable dress for the affair.
options_english.B: She is upset about her husband's reaction.
options_english.C: She is worried about the cost of a suitable costume.
options_english.D: The card did not bear her name.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). There is no mention in the extract of the card not bearing Matilda's name. Her distress stems from having no suitable dress (A), her emotional reaction to her situation (B), and her concern about asking for a sum large enough for a costume without frightening her husband (C). Option D is not mentioned anywhere in the passage and is therefore not a reason for her distress.

sub_questions.text_english: What did Matilda suggest that her husband do with the card?

key_points: Matilda suggested that her husband give the card to some colleague whose wife is better dressed than she is.

sub_questions.solution: Matilda suggested that her husband give the invitation card to some colleague whose wife was better fitted out — that is, better dressed — than herself. This suggestion reflects her deep sense of inadequacy and embarrassment about not having a suitable dress to wear to the affair.

sub_questions.text_english: In the given extract what does the term 'economical clerk' imply?

key_points: The term 'economical clerk' implies that Matilda's husband is a frugal, financially cautious man who is careful with money and does not spend lavishly.

sub_questions.solution: The term 'economical clerk' implies that Matilda's husband is a thrifty and financially careful man. He holds a modest clerical position with a limited salary, and he is known to be cautious about spending money. Matilda is wary of asking for too large a sum, knowing it would alarm him. The word 'economical' here emphasises his frugal nature rather than any skill at managing finances.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract A:
Belinda giggled till she shook the house,
And Blink said Weeck! Which is giggling for a mouse,
Ink and Mustard rudely asked his age,
When Custard cried for a nice safe cage.
Suddenly, suddenly they heard a nasty sound,
And Mustard growled, and they all looked around.
(The Tale of Custard the Dragon)

What inference can be drawn from the repetition of 'suddenly, suddenly' in the above extract?
(A) The scene shook the house
(B) It highlights the swift assault
(C) It emphasises that an unexpected noise was heard
(D) It directs our notice to Mustard's growling

options_english.C: It emphasises that an unexpected noise was heard
options_english.D: It directs our notice to Mustard's growling

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The repetition of 'suddenly, suddenly' is a literary device used to create a sense of shock and urgency. It emphasises the abruptness and unexpectedness of the nasty sound that broke the cheerful mood. Options A, B, and D are not directly supported by what the repetition achieves — the primary effect is to stress how startlingly and without warning the sound appeared.

sub_questions.text_english: Despite its symbolism of captivity, what leads Custard to have a preference for staying in a cage?

key_points: Custard feels unsafe and insecure in the outside world.
He prefers the cage because it offers him a sense of protection and security, despite being mocked by others.

sub_questions.solution: Although a cage symbolises captivity and restriction, Custard prefers it because he feels fundamentally insecure and fearful in the world around him. He is constantly mocked by Belinda, Ink, Mustard, and Blink for his cowardice, yet despite being a dragon, he cannot overcome his deep-seated sense of vulnerability. To Custard, the cage represents safety and protection from the unknown dangers of the outside world.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that applies the same rhyme scheme as the lines of the first four lines of the given extract:
(A) Through the telescope she saw a star / which she thought was very far / She stretched her hand / and felt the crumple of the sand.
(B) Through the telescope she saw a star / She stretched her hand / As it was very far / But felt the crumple of the sand.
(C) Through the telescope she saw a star / Which she thought was very far / Her hand she stretched / But felt the crumple of the sand.
(D) Through the telescope she saw a star / Which she thought was very far / Her hand she stretched afar / But felt the crumple of the sand.

options_english.A: Through the telescope she saw a star / which she thought was very far / She stretched her hand / and felt the crumple of the sand.
options_english.B: Through the telescope she saw a star / She stretched her hand / As it was very far / But felt the crumple of the sand.
options_english.C: Through the telescope she saw a star / Which she thought was very far / Her hand she stretched / But felt the crumple of the sand.
options_english.D: Through the telescope she saw a star / Which she thought was very far / Her hand she stretched afar / But felt the crumple of the sand.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). The first four lines of the extract follow the rhyme scheme AABB — house/mouse rhyme (AA) and age/cage rhyme (BB). Option A follows the same AABB pattern: star/far rhyme (AA) and hand/sand rhyme (BB). Options B and C follow different rhyme patterns, and Option D has a different structure with three rhyming lines in a row.

sub_questions.text_english:
In the given extract,

The difference between the other animals and Custard is that Custard behaves like a _______ (coward / dragon).
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is 'coward'. While Belinda and the other pets — Ink, Mustard, and Blink — display confidence, boldness, and even mockery, Custard cries for a nice safe cage. This behaviour is cowardly, especially for a dragon who is expected to be fierce and brave. The irony of the poem lies in this contrast between Custard's expected nature and his actual timid behaviour.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract B:
I sit inside, doors open to the veranda
writing long letters
in which I scarcely mention the departure
of the forest from the house.
The night is fresh, the whole moon shines
in a sky still open ...... (The Trees)

What atmosphere or mood is created by the language and imagery used in the above lines?

key_points: The atmosphere is calm, open, and quietly contemplative.
The imagery of the open night, moonlight, and open sky creates a mood of peaceful freedom and subtle transition.

sub_questions.solution: The language and imagery in the extract create a calm, serene, and quietly contemplative atmosphere. The image of the poet sitting indoors with doors open to the veranda suggests a gentle boundary between the human and natural worlds. The 'fresh night' and the 'whole moon shining in a sky still open' evoke a mood of peaceful freedom and expansiveness. There is also a subtle undertone of denial and avoidance, as the speaker barely mentions the significant departure of the forest.

sub_questions.text_english:
Choose the option that correctly pairs the two different meanings implied by the use of 'open' twice in the extract:
(A) entry point - vastness
(B) sharing a common space - great view
(C) allowing access and vision - expanse of space
(D) advantage - obstacles ahead

options_english.B: sharing a common space - great view
options_english.C: allowing access and vision - expanse of space

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The first use of 'open' — 'doors open to the veranda' — means allowing access and vision into the outside world. The second use — 'a sky still open' — conveys the expanse of infinite space above. Together, these two meanings suggest a movement from the domestic interior to the boundless natural world. Options A, B, and D do not accurately capture the dual meaning conveyed by the poet.

sub_questions.text_english: From the provided extract, what is conspicuously absent from the long letters the speaker is writing while they sit indoors with the doors open to the veranda?

key_points: The departure of the forest from the house is conspicuously absent from the letters.

sub_questions.solution: What is conspicuously absent from the speaker's long letters is any mention of the departure of the forest from the house. The poet says she 'scarcely mentions' this significant event, suggesting a deliberate avoidance of acknowledging the trees' movement back into nature — a symbol of suppressed natural freedom.

sub_questions.text_english:
How does the poet describe the night?
1. dark  2. frightening  3. dense  4. fresh  5. bright
Select the correct option:
(A) 1 and 5
(B) Only 3
(C) 4 and 5
(D) 2 and 4
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 4 and 5. The poet describes the night as 'fresh' (option 4) and the moon as shining brightly against the sky, which implies a bright night (option 5). The extract reads: 'The night is fresh, the whole moon shines.' Options 1 (dark), 2 (frightening), and 3 (dense) are not supported by the lines of the poem.

sub_questions.text_english: Every creature possesses a unique characteristic that defines it, and this trait is closely linked to its nature. This concept is beautifully illustrated in the poem 'How to Tell Wild Animals.' Elucidate.

key_points: Each animal in the poem is identified by its distinctive and defining trait.
The Bengal Tiger roars and laps blood; the Bear hugs tightly; the Crocodile weeps; the Chameleon has no ears or wings — each trait defines the animal uniquely.

sub_questions.solution: In the poem 'How to Tell Wild Animals', Carolyn Wells humorously illustrates that each wild creature possesses a defining characteristic. The Bengal Tiger is identified by its roaring and violent nature, the Bear by its crushing hug, and the Crocodile by its deceptive weeping. The Chameleon is defined by its ability to change colour. Each trait is inseparable from the animal's identity and nature.

sub_questions.text_english: Pranjal seemed to have a different level of enthusiasm compared to Rajvir when they both saw the tree plantation. Justify. (Glimpses of India)

key_points: Rajvir was excited and enthusiastic upon seeing the tea plantations for the first time.
Pranjal, being familiar with the plantation, was not as enthusiastic — it was a common sight for him.

sub_questions.solution: In 'Glimpses of India — Tea from Assam', Rajvir was thrilled to see the vast green tea plantations for the first time and eagerly shared his knowledge about tea. Pranjal, however, was less enthusiastic as he had grown up in Assam and was completely familiar with the sight. For Pranjal, the plantation was an everyday reality, not a novelty, unlike for the first-time visitor Rajvir.

sub_questions.text_english: In the poem 'Dust of Snow', the 'hemlock tree' and the 'crow' hold specific meanings. Elaborate on how these symbols are utilized within the context of the poem.

key_points: The hemlock tree is traditionally associated with poison and death, symbolising the poet's gloomy and regretful mood.
The crow is a symbol of bad omen and darkness, reinforcing the negative atmosphere.
Together, they contrast with the healing effect of the snow, making the change in mood more significant.

sub_questions.solution: In 'Dust of Snow', Robert Frost uses the hemlock tree and the crow as symbols of gloom and darkness. The hemlock is associated with poison and death, while the crow is traditionally considered a bad omen. Both symbols establish the poet's despondent mood. However, this dark setting ironically becomes the backdrop for a small, uplifting moment — the snow falling from the tree — which saves the rest of his day.

sub_questions.text_english: In what manner did Lencho's cornfield suffer damage? Did he hold any expectations of receiving assistance? (A Letter to God)

key_points: Lencho's cornfield was destroyed by a hailstorm that left nothing behind.
He had absolute faith in God and wrote a letter to God expecting financial assistance of one hundred pesos.

sub_questions.solution: In 'A Letter to God', Lencho's cornfield was completely destroyed by a severe hailstorm. What had looked like a shower of new coins turned into a rain of ice that left the fields looking like a white blanket. Despite the devastating loss, Lencho held unwavering faith in God and wrote a letter requesting one hundred pesos, firmly believing that God would help him and his family survive.

sub_questions.text_english: Engaging in discussions and disputes rarely leads to problem resolution. Support the statement with evidence from the text. (The Proposal)

key_points: In 'The Proposal', Lomov and Natalya constantly quarrel about petty matters instead of completing the marriage proposal.
Their disputes over the Oxen Meadows and the superiority of their dogs prevent any meaningful progress.

sub_questions.solution: In Anton Chekhov's 'The Proposal', Lomov arrives to propose to Natalya, but the conversation repeatedly degenerates into heated arguments — first over the ownership of the Oxen Meadows and then over whose dog is superior. Each dispute prevents the real purpose of the visit from being achieved. This clearly illustrates that endless bickering and disputes lead nowhere and only delay meaningful resolution.

sub_questions.text_english: Bholi's heart was brimming with 'fresh optimism and a renewed existence.' What significance does the expression 'a new hope and a new life' hold for Bholi?

'A new hope and a new life' signifies her transformation — she becomes capable of standing up for herself and refusing an exploitative marriage.

sub_questions.solution: For Bholi, 'a new hope and a new life' signifies a complete transformation of her identity. Once a neglected and stammering child who was pitied by everyone, education at school gave her confidence, self-respect, and a voice. She grows into a courageous young woman who boldly refuses to marry the greedy Bishamber, choosing dignity over social compliance. Education truly became her path to a new existence.

sub_questions.text_english: Lunch transformed into a significant ceremonial event for Mr. Herriot and his associates. Do you agree? Explain with reference to 'A Triumph of Surgery'.

The recovery of the dog was treated as a triumph, and the lunch became a joyful ceremonial celebration among Mr. Herriot and the staff.

sub_questions.solution: Yes, in 'A Triumph of Surgery', when Tricki recovers fully and is ready to return home, Mr. Herriot and his staff celebrate with what becomes a memorable ceremonial lunch. The staff toasts with brandy and enjoy a hearty meal, transforming an ordinary lunch into a celebration of a successful, effortless recovery. For them, Tricki's survival without actual surgery was indeed a triumph worth celebrating together.

When the police knock at the door, Max jumps out of the window expecting to land on this imaginary balcony. There is no balcony, and he falls. Ausable's fabricated tale was a quick-witted strategy to neutralise the threat without any violence.

sub_questions.text_english: Explore the theme of loss as it is depicted in both the 'Ball Poem' and 'The Sermon at Benaras', highlighting the inevitable nature of this aspect in life.

key_points: In 'The Ball Poem', the boy loses his ball and must learn to accept loss as an inevitable part of life.
In 'The Sermon at Benaras', Kisa Gotami loses her son and must accept the universality of death through the Buddha's teaching.
Both texts present loss not as something to be overcome, but to be accepted with maturity and understanding.
Loss leads to emotional and spiritual growth in both texts.
The inevitability of loss is a universal human experience.

sub_questions.solution: Both 'The Ball Poem' by John Berryman and 'The Sermon at Benaras' explore the deeply human theme of loss and the necessity of accepting it. In 'The Ball Poem', a young boy loses his ball and is inconsolable. The poet uses this simple incident to illustrate that loss is an unavoidable part of growing up. The boy must learn that no money can retrieve what is gone — this is his first encounter with irreversible loss, a rite of passage into maturity. In 'The Sermon at Benaras', Kisa Gotami loses her beloved son and is consumed by grief. The Buddha, through his compassionate wisdom, teaches her that death is universal — no house has been spared from it. Both texts present loss not as something to be escaped or denied, but as a fundamental truth of existence. Accepting loss with equanimity leads to emotional and spiritual growth. The inevitable nature of loss, whether of a toy or a loved one, shapes the human experience profoundly.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the similarities and differences between the young seagull from 'Two stories about flying' and Lencho from 'A Letter to God', and provide a rationale for the significant role faith plays in challenging and adverse situations in life.

key_points: Both the young seagull and Lencho face a challenging situation that demands courage and faith.
The young seagull overcomes his fear of flying through necessity and natural instinct.
Lencho overcomes his despair through unshakeable faith in God.
Similarity: both face adversity and emerge transformed.
Difference: the seagull's faith is instinctive and physical, while Lencho's is spiritual and absolute.
Faith — whether in one's own ability or in a higher power — is the driving force that helps both characters overcome their challenges.

sub_questions.solution: The young seagull in 'Two Stories About Flying' and Lencho in 'A Letter to God' are both characters who face adversity and overcome it through faith — albeit of different kinds. The young seagull is paralysed by fear and refuses to take the leap of faith required to fly. However, driven by hunger and the encouragement of his family, he finally spreads his wings and soars. His faith is instinctive — a trust in his own natural ability. Lencho, on the other hand, faces the complete destruction of his crops by a hailstorm. He does not despair but writes a letter directly to God, trusting absolutely in divine support. His faith is spiritual and unwavering. A key similarity is that both characters confront a seemingly insurmountable challenge and emerge transformed. The difference lies in the nature of their faith — one physical and instinctive, the other deeply spiritual. Both stories affirm that faith, whether in oneself or in a higher power, is the most powerful force that enables humans to endure and triumph over adversity.

sub_questions.text_english: Evaluate Griffin's character as a brilliant scientist and a lawless person. (Footprints without Feet)

key_points: Griffin is a brilliant scientist — he discovers the formula for invisibility, a remarkable scientific achievement.
However, he is selfish and uses his discovery not for the good of humanity but for personal gain.
He burns down his landlord's house, robs and assaults innocent people, and is generally violent and antisocial.
His lawlessness stems from his belief that being invisible places him above the law and social norms.
Ultimately, Griffin is a tragic figure — his genius is wasted because of his moral bankruptcy.

sub_questions.solution: Griffin in H.G. Wells' 'Footprints Without Feet' presents a fascinating yet deeply troubling duality. As a scientist, he is undeniably brilliant — his discovery of a drug that can render the human body invisible is a remarkable and extraordinary scientific achievement. It places him among the greatest scientific minds. However, Griffin is simultaneously a deeply flawed and dangerous individual. Rather than using his invention for the benefit of humanity, he employs it purely for selfish and criminal purposes. He sets fire to his landlord's house, breaks into shops to steal food and clothing, robs an old clergyman and his wife, and viciously assaults the landlord of the inn at Iping. His invisibility, instead of being a tool for progress, becomes a weapon of crime. He is arrogant, unempathetic, and believes himself to be above all social and moral laws. His genius, therefore, is ultimately a dangerous gift, wasted on a man who lacks conscience and respect for human life. Griffin is a cautionary reminder that brilliance without ethics can be destructive.

sub_questions.text_english: Half-baked knowledge is always dangerous. Rushing to conclusions without going deep into the details of things always leads to uninvited chaos and disasters. Explain the above mentioned statements in the light of Think-Tank's interpretation of the rhymes in the book 'Mother Goose'. (The Book that saved the Earth)

key_points: Think-Tank misreads the nursery rhymes in Mother Goose due to his arrogance and surface-level understanding.
He interprets 'Mistress Mary' as proof that Earthlings grow explosives.
'Little Miss Muffet' is seen as evidence of Earthlings fighting giant creatures.
'Humpty Dumpty' convinces Think-Tank that Earthlings can predict Martian plans.
This chaos leads him to cancel the invasion and flee Mars.
The story illustrates the danger of drawing conclusions without proper knowledge or context.

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Book that Saved the Earth', Think-Tank's misinterpretation of nursery rhymes from the book 'Mother Goose' is a brilliant comic illustration of the dangers of half-baked knowledge. Think-Tank, despite his enormous ego and claim to supreme intelligence, entirely lacks the cultural context needed to understand Earth's children's literature. He interprets 'Mistress Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow?' as evidence that Earthlings cultivate explosives. 'Little Miss Muffet' convinces him that the people of Earth are engaged in fierce battles with giant insects. Most alarmingly, 'Humpty Dumpty' leads him to believe that Earthlings have already decoded Martian secrets and are preparing to invade Mars. His shallow reading — leaping to dramatic conclusions based on no real understanding — creates panic on Mars and ultimately leads him to call off the entire invasion. The story is a sharp satire on arrogance and the dangers of superficial knowledge. Think-Tank's downfall is not a lack of intelligence but a refusal to seek proper understanding before acting. Rushing to conclusions without depth of knowledge truly leads to unnecessary chaos and disaster.
